crossing supervisor Listen Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Print Content components School crossing supervisors have a much-valued role in Boroondara. On an average school day in Boroondara, they help 9,266 pedestrians to cross the street while 74,426 motor vehicles use our roads during school crossing times. We are always looking for school crossing supervisors. If you are friendly, reliable and flexible, this role is for you. What does a school crossing supervisor do? This paid position gives you the opportunity to get involved in your community and improve road safety for children, people with a disability and the general public who use our 114 school crossings. School crossing supervisors: • work part-time Monday to Friday, from 8 am to 9 am and from 3 pm to 4 pm, during the school term • play an important role in educating children with ‘Stop, Look and Listen’ instructions • are responsible for reporting any road hazards or potential risks • help to encourage active and independent travel. About you We are looking for people aged 18 and older who: • can attend shifts at short notice • have their own reliable transport • are able to work across several locations • can complete the pre-employment medical and police checks. You will have access to a full training program before starting your role. Download the position description School Crossing Supervisor PD 144.04 KB [PDF] 23 November 2022 How to apply Learn more about this rewarding role by reading the position description above. Submit an online application through our Careers website . Attend an interview – meet with one of our Council Officers at Council, located at 8 Inglesby Road in Camberwell. Provide us with relevant employment documents – including your Working With Children Check, Police Check and evidence of your COVID-19 vaccination status. Complete a medical assessment. Apply to become a School Crossings Supervisor We are always recruiting new school crossing supervisors to help people to cross our roads safely at peak school times. Non-hybrid position. 12-month fixed contract (with opportunity to extend). Prime leadership opportunity for an individual passionate about creating positive workplace culture and delivering industry-leading service standards. The role places you at the helm of a specialised team of compliance officers, providing a service highly valued by our community. A little bit about the role City of Boroondara is a leader in the Local Government sector and one of the nation’s most liveable municipal councils. The Team Leader Compliance plays a key role in the leadership of the Civic Services Department, which deliver multiple regulatory services to protect the health, safety, amenity and assets of the city. Our department is a hive of activity with the highest customer interface in Council and no two days will be the same. Reporting to the Coordinator Compliance Programs and supported by an experienced senior leadership team, key responsibilities include: Lead, supervise and support a multi-disciplined team of Local Laws and Animal Management Officers. Drive high standards of investigative practices and service excellence through coaching and mentoring of Officers to enable their success. Foster an innovative, engaged, customer-focused and high performing team. Shape a workplace culture underpinned by our core workplace values. Contribute to the broader, strategic compliance matters across the Department - including public health, construction and parking. Lead by example to provide exemplary customer service. Provide relevant technical advice and manage escalated matters by managing up to senior leadership to provide recommendations to resolve high-profile cases. Coordinate rosters and allocate tasks according to service requirements. A fully maintained vehicle is provided as 'tool of trade' to perform necessary duties and commute to and from work. A little bit about you Your skills are the foundation of our success. The skills and experience you bring: Experienced people leader with a passion for working with others and developing your teams to reach their full potential. High emotional intelligence and an empathic approach with demonstrated ability to maintain positive relationships and communicate effectively. Demonstrated ability to support, inspire, build and develop a strong team with robust, consistent team-work practices. Customer focused with demonstrated ability to promptly resolve issues and communicate outcomes. Critical thinking skills to be able to break down a problem and arrive at a position that is legally sound and meets community expectations. Experience in a regulatory role previously is preferred but not mandatory. People with strong customer service, retail and hospitality leadership backgrounds transition very successfully into this role. Want to know more? To connect further and gain a better insight into this opportunity view the Position Description What sets us apart? An investment in your ongoing professional and personal development including inhouse and external leadership programs and growth and secondment opportunities. Your potential is recognised and your career trajectory is a shared priority The Civic Service’s Department is evolving, and this is an exciting time to join us in re-shaping our function and playing a significant part in an exceptionally large-scale transformation You will be part of a team that makes a real difference. Working at Boroondara means contributing to creating positive change in the world. Join us in a role where your work matters, and you contribute to meaningful outcomes A supportive and friendly workplace culture that values diversity, collaboration and continuous improvement We offer many staff benefits such as flexible working arrangements, study support, wellbeing programs, gym and pool memberships Employment requirements Current Victorian Driver’s Licence Applicants must have the right to work in Australia. Preferred applicants will be required to undergo a National Police Record Check How to apply Please submit your application online via the ‘Apply’ button by Friday 2 October 2026, 11:59pm . For any confidential discussion please contact Harry Mellos, Coordinator Compliance Programs on 041 196 127. We understand that this portal may not meet the needs of people who rely on Assistive Technology or have other diverse requirements. If you have any difficulty using our recruitment system, please do not hesitate to contact People Culture and Development on (03) 9278 4401 or pcd@boroondara.vic.gov.au to allow us to help in any way we can. Who are we? The City of Boroondara is a metropolitan council, representing more than 170,000 people in the inner-eastern suburbs of Melbourne. A leader in the local government sector, with a reputation for innovation and excellence, we believe in providing an environment where our staff thrive, both in the work they do and in how they learn and develop as people and professionals. We like to challenge the norm and we are investing significantly in innovation and technology improvements in order to provide our customers with an even greater experience and engagement. We are putting our customers at the forefront of what we do with our organisation wide initiative, Transforming Boroondara Program. You will be instrumental in driving this change across the organisation using best practice approaches to successfully support us from the now to our desired future state. Skip to Main Content Career Opportunities: Local Laws Officer (15251) Requisition ID 15251 - Posted - Job Function (1) - Tenure Status (1) - Employment Status (1)  Job Description Print Preview Apply Save Job Email Job to Friend Return to List Local Laws Officer Join a dynamic, investigations team that supports each other to succeed Deliver meaningful outcomes to the community in safety and amenity $93,845 -101,184 per annum (plus super) Tool of trade vehicle provided (non-hybrid position) Join us in building a professional investigations team and help deliver a responsive, community-focused Local Laws service. In this role, you will contribute to a safe, liveable and well-maintained municipality while providing high-quality regulatory service to residents and stakeholders. About the role At City of Boroondara, our Local Laws directly contributes to our purpose of protecting the health, safety, amenity and assets of the municipality. Based within the large and busy department of Civic Services, the team works as part of five field-based teams and many others within the Urban Living Directorate. You will respond to reported breaches of the Amenity Local Law and the Environment Protection Act, using education, investigation and enforcement to achieve compliance. The role involves managing a varied caseload, gathering evidence, preparing clear records and working within established procedures to resolve matters fairly and effectively. The position includes investigating issues such as illegally dumped rubbish under the EPA, unsightly properties, overhanging vegetation, illegally advertising and the occupation of Council land, while providing courteous and timely service to community members. From time to time, you will also support the Animal Management team with park patrols, and work with external stakeholders including Victoria Police, the Magistrates’ Court and Council prosecutors. Hours are allocated over a 16-week roster (42-hours per week) and rotating weekend work is required every 4 weeks with penalty rates that convert into an annualised salary. A fully maintained vehicle is provided as a ‘tool of trade’ to perform necessary duties and commute to and from work. This is a non-hybrid role as our ‘office’ is in the community, every day and our success comes from working together with other officers, as a team! About you We are looking for someone who brings sound judgement, a strong customer focus and a collaborative approach. You will be supported to build your knowledge and succeed in the role. You will have experience delivering customer service in a complex regulatory environment or another fast-paced setting, with the ability to communicate clearly, build rapport and respond professionally in a range of situations under pressure. Experience in areas such as retail, hospitality, community services or other enforcement role can provide a strong foundation for success in this role. You will be able to investigate issues methodically, collect information accurately and prepare clear notes and reports. Knowledge of compliance, local laws or related legislation will be well regarded, as will the ability to interpret policy and apply it in practical situations. If you are still developing in these areas, a willingness to learn will be equally valued. Success in this role also requires respectful negotiation skills, sound problem-solving and judgement skills, de-escalating interpersonal situations with members of the community, and the capacity to work across the community each day, including walking for extended periods and assisting with animal handling when required. A qualification in enforcement, local laws, justice or a related field is desirable, but not essential. Want to know more? View the Position description What sets us apart? An investment in your ongoing professional and personal development You will be part of a team that makes a real difference. Working at Boroondara means contributing to creating positive change in the world. Join us in a role where your work matters, and you contribute to meaningful outcomes. A supportive and friendly workplace culture that values diversity, collaboration and continuous improvement. We offer many staff benefits such as flexible working arrangements, study support, wellbeing programs, gym and pool memberships Employment requirements Applicants must have the right to work in Australia. Preferred applicants will be required to undergo a National Police Record Check. All City of Boroondara employees must be fully vaccinated. Appointment of the successful candidate will be subject to provision of evidence of vaccination status or medical exemption prior to commencement. How to Apply Follow these steps, carefully: Please submit your application online via the ‘ Apply ’ button by Friday 2 October 2026 11:59pm . Ensure you address your cover letter to Harry Mellos and answer the following questions: What about the Local Laws Officer role motivates you? Why is this the next logical step in your career? All applications must be made via the online portal; no applications direct to the hiring manager will be considered. No calls or applications from agencies please. For any confidential discussion please contact Harry Mellos, Coordinator Compliance Programs (during business hours) on 0421 196 127. We understand that this portal may not meet the needs of people who rely on Assistive Technology or have other diverse requirements. If you have any difficulty using our recruitment system, please do not hesitate to contact People Culture and Development on (03) 9278 4401 or pcd@boroondara.vic.gov.au to allow us to help in any way we can. Who are we? The City of Boroondara is a metropolitan council, representing more than 170,000 people in the inner-eastern suburbs of Melbourne. A leader in the local government sector, with a reputation for innovation and excellence, we believe in providing an environment where our staff thrive, both in the work they do and in how they learn and develop as people and professionals. We like to challenge the norm and we are investing significantly in innovation and technology improvements in order to provide our customers with an even greater experience and engagement. We are putting our customers at the forefront of what we do with our organisation wide initiative, Transforming Boroondara Program. You will be instrumental in driving this change across the organisation using best practice approaches to successfully support us from the now to our desired future state. Skip to Main Content Career Opportunities: Maternal & Child Health Coordinator (15211) Requisition ID 15211 - Posted - Job Function (1) - Tenure Status (1) - Employment Status (1)  Job Description Print Preview Apply Save Job Email Job to Friend Return to List Maternal & Child Health Coordinator Lead a high-quality Maternal and Child Health service that makes a lasting difference to children and families Full time permanent position based in Camberwell but expected to work across other Boroondara locations. $148,715 MCH Coordinator salary plus Superannuation plus RDO. At the City of Boroondara, our vision is a healthy, connected and sustainable community. We are seeking an experienced and passionate Maternal & Child Health (MCH) Coordinator to lead our Maternal and Child Health Service and help shape the future of early years outcomes for our community. This is a significant leadership opportunity for an accomplished MCH professional who thrives on building high-performing teams, driving clinical excellence and delivering contemporary, family-centred services. About the role Reporting to the Senior Coordinator Community Wellbeing, you will provide strategic, operational and clinical governance leadership for Council's Maternal and Child Health Service. Leading a team of dedicated professionals, you will be responsible for ensuring the delivery of safe, high-quality, evidence-based and responsive services for children and families across Boroondara. As a member of the Community Wellbeing Leadership Team, you will work collaboratively across Council and with external partners to support integrated early years, child safety and community wellbeing outcomes. Key responsibilities include: Leading the strategic planning, delivery and continuous improvement of Maternal and Child Health services. Providing workforce leadership, capability development and succession planning for the MCH team. Driving clinical governance, quality improvement, risk management and evidence-based practice. Overseeing Universal and Enhanced Maternal and Child Health programs. Managing service performance, budgets, grants and funding requirements. Ensuring compliance with Victorian MCH frameworks, legislative requirements and professional standards. Leading implementation of child safety, family violence, safeguarding and information sharing requirements. Building strong partnerships across the health, early years and community sectors. Providing expert advice on emerging issues, service reform and strategic opportunities. About you You are a respected clinical leader with a strong understanding of Maternal and Child Health services and contemporary early years practice. You bring the ability to balance strategic thinking with operational leadership, while fostering a positive and high-performing team culture. To be successful, you will have: Current AHPRA registration as a Registered Nurse and Registered Midwife, with recognised qualifications in Maternal and Child Health Nursing. Significant leadership experience within a clinical, health or human services environment. Comprehensive knowledge of the Victorian Universal and Enhanced Maternal and Child Health Service Framework. Experience in clinical governance, quality improvement, risk management and service innovation. Strong understanding of child safety, family violence, MARAM and related safeguarding requirements. Demonstrated success in workforce planning, recruitment, performance management and organisational change. Experience managing budgets, funding programs, performance reporting and service delivery outcomes. Exceptional communication, stakeholder engagement and influencing skills. A commitment to delivering equitable, family-centred services that improve outcomes for children and families. Why join us? At Boroondara, you'll be part of a values-driven organisation committed to supporting our community and our people. Our values guide how we work every day: Innovate | Integrity | Respect | Own It | Collaborate | Customer We offer: A meaningful leadership role with significant community impact. A supportive and collaborative leadership environment. Professional development and continuous learning opportunities. Flexible and inclusive workplace practices. The opportunity to lead a highly regarded Maternal and Child Health service. Employment Requirements The successful applicant will be required to hold: Current AHPRA registration as a Registered Nurse and Registered Midwife. Recognised Maternal and Child Health Nursing qualifications. Current Driver Licence. Current National Police Check. Current Employee Working with Children Check (or ability to obtain one). The City of Boroondara is a child safe organisation with zero tolerance for child abuse, neglect or harm. We are committed to creating and maintaining a child-safe environment for all children and young people. Apply now If you are an experienced Maternal and Child Health leader ready to shape the future of services for children and families in Boroondara, we'd love to hear from you. Please submit your application online via the ‘Apply’ button by 11:59pm Thursday 24th September 2026 . All applications must be made via the online portal. For any further information please refer to the Position Description , or contact Penelope Shaw ( Senior Coordinator Community Wellbeing ) during business hours on 9278 4712 for a confidential discussion. We understand that this portal may not meet the needs of people who rely on Assistive Technology or have other diverse requirements. If you have any difficulty using our recruitment system, please do not hesitate to contact People Culture and Development on (03) 9278 4401 or pcd@boroondara.vic.gov.au to allow us to help in any way we can. Who are we? The City of Boroondara is a metropolitan council, representing more than 170,000 people in the inner-eastern suburbs of Melbourne. A leader in the local government sector, with a reputation for innovation and excellence, we believe in providing an environment where our staff thrive, both in the work they do and in how they learn and develop as people and professionals. We like to challenge the norm and we are investing significantly in innovation and technology improvements in order to provide our customers with an even greater experience and engagement. We are putting our customers at the forefront of what we do with our organisation wide initiative, Transforming Boroondara Program. You will be instrumental in driving this change across the organisation using best practice approaches to successfully support us from the now to our desired future state. Full-time permanent position $104,790- $114, 015 Band 6 plus Superannuation plus RDO At the City of Boroondara, we're committed to creating a healthy, connected and sustainable community. We're seeking an experienced and motivated Community Wellbeing Administration Lead to oversee the administration of our highly regarded Immunisation Service and support the delivery of essential public health programs to our community. This is an exciting opportunity for a collaborative leader who enjoys improving systems, supporting people and ensuring services run efficiently and effectively. About the Role Reporting to the Community Wellbeing Senior Coordinator, you will lead a small administration team responsible for supporting Council's Immunisation Service. You'll play a key role in coordinating vaccination programs, managing service administration, overseeing systems and processes, and ensuring compliance with relevant legislative and public health requirements. Working closely with nurses, Maternal and Child Health teams, schools, community groups and government agencies, you'll help deliver high-quality services that support the health and wellbeing of Boroondara residents. Key responsibilities include: Leading the day-to-day administration of Council's Immunisation Service. Coordinating school, community, workplace and staff vaccination programs. Overseeing rostering, service systems, reporting and data quality. Managing contracts, procurement processes and budget monitoring. Supporting continuous improvement initiatives and service innovation. Leading and developing a high-performing administration team. Building strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders. Contributing to public health emergency preparedness and response activities. About You You are an organised and proactive people leader with strong administrative and operational management skills. You enjoy improving processes, solving problems and working collaboratively in a dynamic environment. You will bring: Demonstrated experience leading and supervising a team. Strong organisational and administrative management skills. Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement abilities. Experience managing budgets, systems and operational processes. The ability to interpret legislation, guidelines and policy requirements. Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills. A commitment to quality service delivery and continuous improvement. Experience within community health, public health, local government or a similar service environment will be highly regarded. Why Join Us? At Boroondara, you'll be part of an organisation that values innovation, collaboration, integrity and customer service. We offer: A supportive and inclusive workplace culture. Opportunities for professional development and growth. Meaningful work that positively impacts the community. Flexible and collaborative working arrangements. The opportunity to contribute to important public health outcomes for our community. If you're a motivated leader who thrives on creating efficient services, supporting teams and delivering positive community outcomes, we'd love to hear from you. Apply now Applications must be submitted via Council's online recruitment portal. Please submit your application online via the ‘Apply’ button by 11:59pm Thursday 01st October 2026. All applications must be made via the online portal. For any further information please refer to the position description or contact Penelope Shaw (Senior Coordinator Community Wellbeing) during business hours on 9278 4712 for a confidential discussion. At the City of Boroondara, we celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued, respected and supported. If you have any difficulty using our recruitment system, please do not hesitate to contact People Culture and Development on (03) 9278 4401 or pcd@boroondara.vic.gov.au to allow us to help in any way we can. Who are we? The City of Boroondara is a metropolitan council, representing more than 170,000 people in the inner-eastern suburbs of Melbourne. A leader in the local government sector, with a reputation for innovation and excellence, we believe in providing an environment where our staff thrive, both in the work they do and in how they learn and develop as people and professionals. We like to challenge the norm and we are investing significantly in innovation and technology improvements in order to provide our customers with an even greater experience and engagement. Do you have experience managing volunteers, coordinating events and building strong community partnerships? The Boroondara Volunteer Resource Centre (BVRC) is seeking an enthusiastic and experienced Diversity & Inclusion Project Officer (Volunteering) to lead an exciting Volunteer Management Activity (VMA) project focused on reducing barriers to volunteering and helping community organisations create more inclusive volunteer programs. This role provides a unique opportunity to influence the future of volunteering by supporting organisations to engage and retain volunteers from diverse backgrounds while strengthening community connections and social inclusion. About the Role Reporting to the Volunteer Support and Development Lead, you will coordinate initiatives that increase participation in volunteering among: Young people aged 12 to 18 People with disability and/or mental health challenges Vulnerable women People experiencing unemployment First Nations peoples Newly arrived migrants Working within the BVRC, you will collaborate with volunteer-involving organisations, community groups, Council staff and sector partners to deliver projects, training, events and resources that support inclusive volunteering practices. What You'll Be Doing Deliver a flagship diversity and inclusion volunteering event featuring expert speakers and lived-experience perspectives. Recruit, train and support Volunteer Ambassadors who promote volunteering within the community. Design and facilitate workshops, learning programs and capacity-building initiatives for volunteer-involving organisations. Develop practical resources, communications and promotional materials that encourage inclusive volunteer engagement. Build strong relationships with community organisations, First Nations groups, multicultural organisations, faith-based groups and sector networks. Conduct outreach activities at community events, neighbourhood houses, schools, libraries and other community settings. Support organisations to develop accessible and inclusive volunteer programs that attract and retain diverse volunteers. Contribute to the growth and visibility of the BVRC and increase participation in volunteering across priority communities. About You We're looking for an innovative and community-focused professional who can build strong relationships and deliver meaningful outcomes. You will bring: Experience managing volunteers and an understanding of current and emerging volunteering trends. Experience planning and delivering community events, workshops or capacity-building programs. Strong project management skills with the ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines. Demonstrated experience developing communications, marketing materials and engagement strategies for diverse audiences. Excellent stakeholder engagement skills and a proven ability to influence and collaborate with community organisations and internal stakeholders. Strong written, verbal and presentation skills. A genuine commitment to diversity, equity, accessibility and inclusion. Qualifications (or current study) in community development, social sciences, human services or a related field. Why Join Us? This is an opportunity to: Lead projects that create lasting community impact. Work with passionate professionals committed to inclusive volunteering. Build strong partnerships across the community sector. Develop innovative programs that improve access to volunteering opportunities. Contribute to a more connected, welcoming and inclusive community. Requirements Successful applicants will be required to hold or obtain: Current Working with Children Check (Employee) National Police Check Apply Now If you're passionate about creating inclusive communities and empowering people from diverse backgrounds to participate in volunteering, we'd love to hear from you. Please submit your application online via the ‘Apply’ button by 11:59pm Tuesday 29th September 2026 . All applications must be made via the online portal. For any further information please refer to the position description or contact Cassandra Chatwin-Smith ( Volunteer Support and Development Lead ) during business hours on 9278 4763 for a confidential discussion. We understand that this portal may not meet the needs of people who rely on Assistive Technology or have other diverse requirements. If you have any difficulty using our recruitment system, please do not hesitate to contact People Culture and Development on (03) 9278 4401 or pcd@boroondara.vic.gov.au to allow us to help in any way we can. Who are we? The City of Boroondara is a metropolitan council, representing more than 170,000 people in the inner-eastern suburbs of Melbourne. A leader in the local government sector, with a reputation for innovation and excellence, we believe in providing an environment where our staff thrive, both in the work they do and in how they learn and develop as people and professionals. We like to challenge the norm and we are investing significantly in innovation and technology improvements in order to provide our customers with an even greater experience and engagement. We are putting our customers at the forefront of what we do with our organisation wide initiative, Transforming Boroondara Program. You will be instrumental in driving this change across the organisation using best practice approaches to successfully support us from the now to our desired future state. This is an exciting opportunity to build relationships with volunteer-involving organisations, support community engagement initiatives, and help deliver services that strengthen and grow volunteering across Boroondara. Working within the Boroondara Volunteer Resource Centre (BVRC ) , you will play a key role in supporting member organisations, coordinating engagement activities, delivering communications, and contributing to events that connect volunteers with valuable opportunities within our community. About us At Boroondara, we are committed to creating a healthy, connected and sustainable community. We place our customers at the centre of everything we do and are guided by our values: Innovate | Integrity | Respect | Own It | Collaborate | Customer About the role Reporting to the Volunteer Support and Development Lead, you will: Build and maintain strong relationships with BVRC member organisations and volunteer-involving organisations. Drive participation in BVRC programs, events and capacity-building opportunities. Support member retention and engagement initiatives. Coordinate and deliver Member Network Meetings and other engagement activities. Develop and distribute member communications, including e-bulletins and social media content. Maintain accurate membership and insurance records within BVRC systems. Support delivery of key events including: Boroondara Volunteer Expo Skilled Volunteer Meet International Volunteer Day Community pop-up activities Respond to enquiries from members and the wider community in line with Council's Customer Promise. Contribute to service planning and continuous improvement initiatives. About you You are a relationship-focused professional who enjoys engaging with diverse stakeholders and making a positive impact in the community. You will bring: A commitment to delivering exceptional customer service. Experience working with community-based organisations, volunteer programs or community development initiatives. Strong relationship-building and stakeholder engagement skills. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. The ability to manage competing priorities and work independently. Confidence using databases, online systems, Microsoft Office and social media platforms. An understanding of volunteering and community development principles and practices. Why join us? Work in a role that makes a genuine difference to the community. Be part of a supportive and collaborative Community Development team. Help strengthen local volunteering and community participation. Enjoy meaningful work with opportunities to contribute to high-profile volunteer and community events. Join an organisation that values innovation, collaboration and customer service. Employment Requirements The successful applicant will be required to provide: A current National Police Check. A current Employee Working with Children Check. The City of Boroondara is a Child Safe organisation and is committed to the safety, wellbeing and inclusion of all children and young people. How to Apply Please submit your application online via the ‘Apply’ button. All applications must be made via the online portal by Thursday 24 September 2026 at 11:59pm. For any further information please refer to the Position Description or contact Cassandra Chatwin-Smith business hours on (03) 9278 4763 for a confidential discussion. We understand that this portal may not meet the needs of people who rely on Assistive Technology or have other diverse requirements. If you have any difficulty using our recruitment system, please do not hesitate to contact People Culture and Development on (03) 9278 4401 or pcd@boroondara.vic.gov.au to allow us to help in any way we can. Who are we? The City of Boroondara is a metropolitan council, representing more than 170,000 people in the inner-eastern suburbs of Melbourne. A leader in the local government sector, with a reputation for innovation and excellence, we believe in providing an environment where our staff thrive, both in the work they do and in how they learn and develop as people and professionals. We like to challenge the norm and we are investing significantly in innovation and technology improvements in order to provide our customers with an even greater experience and engagement. We are putting our customers at the forefront of what we do with our organisation wide initiative, Transforming Boroondara Program. You will be instrumental in driving this change across the organisation using best practice approaches to successfully support us from the now to our desired future state. About the role Reporting to the Team Leader Sportsgrounds, you will: Undertake sportsground maintenance, mowing, turf renovations and irrigation works. We are seeking skilled and experienced professional care workers who love supporting people to live independently in the community. We currently provide services in Mount Alexander Shire and Central Goldfields Shire. This is your opportunity to bring your passion and skills to be part of a professional and dedicated team providing high quality in-home support to frail older people and people with disabilities in our community. The role provides tailored services to help clients live healthy, independent and active lives through assistance with daily tasks and activities. Direct Care Worker Traineeship Opportunities: If you don’t already have a certificate III in Individual Support, you can also apply here for a Trainee Direct Care Worker position, to earn and learn on the job. Minimum Qualifications and Experience You must have, or be willing to obtain: Current Police Check Current Working with Children Check Triple vaccinated for COVID (2 doses plus a booster). Current Drivers license and roadworthy, registered and comprehensively insured vehicle for work travel Applicants must be able to work weekends. First Aid and CPR certificate will be gained though training and applied to the role as required If you have any queries or would like to discuss the role, the key contacts are: Sarah Newstead In Home Support Coordinator – East (03) 5471 1845 Talia Jenkin In Home Support Coordinator – West (03) 5471 1728 To apply for a Direct Care Worker or Direct Care Worker Trainee position, please provide a cover letter (no more than 2 pages) outlining why you are interested and the best candidate for this role, and your current resume. Additional information Mount Alexander Shire Council is committed to providing a safe, inclusive, and respectful workplace. We are an equal opportunity employer and are committed to child safety with zero tolerance for child abuse. We value a diverse workforce and encourage applicants from all cultures, sexual orientations, gender identities and backgrounds. Applicants can expect that the recruitment process will include interviewing, reference checks and criminal history checks. Some positions will also be required to provide a Working with Children Check, and medical assessments including drug and alcohol testing may be undertaken. For more information on the recruitment process, please download the Candidate information document from our website.
